entities.name: California State University, Fresno
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
California State University, Fresno (Fresno State, founded 1911) is the oldest California State University campus after the first normal schools — located in Fresno, the commercial center of California's Central Valley, the world's most productive agricultural region — and serving the San Joaquin Valley's largely agricultural economy and increasingly diverse population, with significant programs in agriculture, viticulture and enology, and agricultural sciences that reflect its unique position as the university of America's most important farming region.

Fresno and the San Joaquin Valley are extraordinary in American agriculture: the region produces over half of the nation's fruits, nuts, and vegetables, making California (and specifically the Central Valley) the world's most diverse and productive agricultural region. Fresno State's agricultural programs — particularly its Jordan College of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, viticulture and enology program, and food science programs — serve the educational needs of an industry that is foundational to American and global food supply.

Fresno State's student body is one of California's most diverse CSU campuses, reflecting the San Joaquin Valley's large Mexican-American community (descended from generations of agricultural workers who settled as the crops changed from seasonal to permanent), Hmong community (one of the largest US Hmong populations outside Minnesota), and other agricultural worker communities. The university's social mobility metrics reflect its role in educating first-generation students from agricultural worker families into professional careers.
